sections.description: The story split into ordered beats — one narrated/spoken film clip each. Order = final screen order.

id.description: Sequential: scene_1, scene_2 … MUST use this exact form (not 's01') — the runner parses the scene number from it.

emotion.description: The ONE feeling the audience should have during this section (e.g. 'curiosity', 'unease', 'comic relief', 'quiet dread', 'acceptance'). Authored as a coherent film-wide emotional arc BEFORE locations/events are chosen; every later stage (framing, lighting, motion, score) serves this value.

text.description: The actual story PROSE for this section, kept intact for reading (2–4 short paragraphs, blank-line separated). Displayed verbatim — do NOT summarise it away.

caption.description: Short place/moment label, e.g. 'Dawn, the gallery rail'.

sceneBrief.description: The key visual EVENT/ACTION this section's shot(s) depict — name the action as the subject (e.g. 'a fist knocks on the door'), never a character before the story has introduced them. Prose, not a prompt.

entities.description: Bible ids (characters/locations/objects) VISIBLE across this section's shots — re-injected into shot prompts.

mode.description: 'dialogue' iff a character SPEAKS in this beat — the story gives them a line, direct or faithfully-converted reported speech; otherwise 'narration'. Classified honestly from the story: a dialogue-rich story correctly yields mostly dialogue sections.

spokenLines.description: Exact spoken-word ledger for this section, carried forward DETERMINISTICALLY by plan.assemble_keyframes from the scene outline (never re-authored by a model, so it cannot drift). This is the authoritative source the scene_video_prompt pass copies its own spokenLines from. It is REQUIRED for a narration-mode section that is voiced: scene_detail may not put dialogue on a narration section's shots, so this ledger is the ONLY path those words have to the render -- without it the video-prompt pass has nothing to copy and invents the narration. Empty/absent means genuinely wordless.

shots.description: FLAT list of every shot across every section (targetShotCount per section, usually 1-3). Each shot is rendered as its OWN independent 4-10s clip; clips are concatenated, never chained or interpolated. Order = cut order.

id.description: MUST be 'scene_<sectionNumber>_shot_<shotNumber>' — e.g. the 2nd shot of scene_3 is 'scene_3_shot_2'. The runner keys first-frame images and audio by this exact id.

characterPresence.description: Which anchors the video-prompt stage lists as this shot's references[], and how it composes the frame. 'character' = an anchored/recurring character must appear recognizably (continuity reaction shots, beats about a person). 'none' = NO recurring character may appear in frame — a pure action/environment/object moment. The model always receives at least one reference, so 'none' is a promise about the frame's content, not a mechanical guarantee.

scene.description: The section number this shot belongs to.

shotNumber.description: 1-based position of this shot within its section.

duration.description: Seconds this shot runs, 2-10 (working range 4-10). Hard 10s ceiling — the runner clamps and snaps to the 4n+1 frame grid at 24fps.

description.description: The ONE distinct ACTION/EVENT this shot shows, verb-first and concrete (e.g. 'a fist pounds three times on the iron door') — NOT a character standing or looking. Omit any character not yet introduced by the story. This is what the shot's video prompt is built from.

cameraWork.description: Optional short framing/camera note (e.g. 'low angle, slow push-in').

dialogue.description: ONLY on shots within a mode='dialogue' section. The exact line spoken during THIS shot, verbatim, one speaker's utterance. A speaker change is a new shot. This is the sole source of the spoken line reaching the video model.

speaker.description: ONLY alongside `dialogue`. The bible character id who speaks this shot's line. The film is silent, so this selects the anchor identity and tells the video-prompt stage whose body language carries the beat; it drives no lip-sync.

emotion.description: ONLY alongside `dialogue`. Short delivery descriptor (e.g. 'warm, tender') feeding the 'in a <emotion> voice' phrasing. Never the spoken words themselves.

motionIntensity.description: NOT USED in this bundle. Shot pacing is expressed through `duration` instead — a multi-stage physical beat earns 8-10s rather than extra keyframe guides.

keyframeCount.description: NOT USED in this bundle (no keyframe chain).

speakerOnScreen.description: NOT USED in this bundle — it existed to protect LTX lip-sync, and this film is silent.

narration_section_ids.description: Subset of `sections[].id` with mode='narration', in section order. MUST exactly match. If the project's `narration` flag is false, MUST be an empty array regardless of section modes.

character_shot_ids.description: Subset of `shots[].id` with characterPresence='character', in shot order. MUST exactly match. Computed for inspection/filtering only — every shot goes through the same Bernini renderer; the shot's video prompt is what enforces the 'none' exclusion.

none_shot_ids.description: Subset of `shots[].id` with characterPresence='none', in shot order. MUST exactly match. Computed for inspection/filtering only — every shot goes through the same Bernini renderer; the shot's video prompt is what enforces the 'none' exclusion.

kf1_shot_ids.description: NOT USED in this bundle — retained only because plan.assemble_keyframes emits it. There is no keyframe chain here: Bernini animates each shot directly from its reference anchors, so this stays empty.

kf2_shot_ids.description: NOT USED in this bundle — retained only because plan.assemble_keyframes emits it. There is no keyframe chain here: Bernini animates each shot directly from its reference anchors, so this stays empty.

kf3_shot_ids.description: NOT USED in this bundle — retained only because plan.assemble_keyframes emits it. There is no keyframe chain here: Bernini animates each shot directly from its reference anchors, so this stays empty.
